title: HTTPStackPolicy
description: Data-driven HTTP-framework selection discipline consumed by the oya-dev-cli `http-stack` gate. Codifies the strategic hyper/axum split (ADR-0090 Amendment 2026-05-29 + ADR-0509 §6): hyper is the PREFERRED low-level default; axum is a SANCTIONED strategic exception that requires a recorded per-crate justification; all other HTTP frameworks are FORBIDDEN (hard fail). The gate reads each workspace member's [dependencies]/[dev-dependencies]/[build-dependencies], detects declared HTTP frameworks, and classifies them against this file. This file is the SINGLE source of truth so the policy is data-driven, not hard-coded in Rust.

_meta.policy_source: docs/decisions/ADR-0705-product-protocol-live-apex.md (Amendment 2026-05-29: strategic hyper/axum split) + docs/decisions/ADR-0709-general-live-apex.md §6 (Canonical service layout: rest/ # axum) + approved-runtime-dependency-allowlist (Hyper/hyper-util/Axum/Tower/tower-http/Tokio blessed)
_meta.purpose: Authoritative HTTP-framework selection policy: hyper preferred (low-level default), axum sanctioned-with-justification, all others forbidden.
_meta.founder_direction_2026_05_29: axum is ok ... hyper preferred (low level preferred) where it makes sense. be strategic about axum and hyper use. enforce/codify it.

preferred_frameworks.note: Low-level default. Use bare hyper (+ the Layer-5 oya-http-runtime-hyper-adapter and the std-only router/middleware/sse kernels) for performance/latency-critical data-plane services, proxies & gateways, hot paths, minimal-dependency or long-LTS-surface crates, and anywhere we want to own the routing/middleware kernel. This is ADR-0090's original thesis and it STANDS. On a toss-up between hyper and axum, choose hyper.

sanctioned_frameworks.note: Strategic exception. Use axum for control-plane / CRUD-heavy REST services with many endpoints + extractors where axum's router/extractor/FromRequest ergonomics materially cut complexity vs hand-rolled hyper (ADR-0509 §6 prescribes `rest/ # axum`). axum is built on hyper + tower, so it rides the same blessed backbone. Any crate that declares `axum` MUST have a recorded rationale in `justified_crates.axum` below, else the gate WARNs (nudging back to the low-level default). tower / tower-http are axum's middleware stack and do not themselves require a justification.

forbidden_frameworks.note: Hard FAIL. These bring framework-competition with our own router/middleware kernels and/or substantially larger transitive trees; ADR-0090's rejection reasoning applies in full. Zero on-dev crates declare any of these as of 2026-05-29, so enforcement is fail-closed from day one.

axum.oya-identity-workload-rest: Identity workload REST surface: many OIDC/OAuth2/SCIM endpoints + typed extractors; axum's router/FromRequest ergonomics materially reduce handler boilerplate vs hand-rolled hyper. Control-plane REST, not a hot data path. ADR-0509 §6 rest/ mod.
axum.oya-cloud-intelligence-rest: Cloud-intelligence REST adapter: multi-endpoint analytics/inference control surface; axum routing + extractors. Control-plane REST, not a latency-critical data path. ADR-0509 §6 rest/ mod.
axum.oya-cloud-intelligence-app: Cloud-intelligence application composition: wires the axum rest router into the service binary. ADR-0509 §6 app/main composition.
axum.oya-managed-k8s-control-plane-host-app: Managed-k8s control-plane host application: control-plane CRUD/admission REST surface; axum router composition. ADR-0376/ADR-0509 §6 rest/ mod.
axum.oya-managed-k8s-cluster-lifecycle-app: Managed-k8s cluster-lifecycle application: control-plane lifecycle REST surface (create/scale/drain/delete); axum router. Control-plane, not a hot path. ADR-0376/ADR-0509 §6.
axum.oya-managed-k8s-tenant-quota-app: Managed-k8s tenant-quota application: control-plane quota admission/reporting REST surface; axum router. Control-plane, not a hot path. ADR-0509 §6.
axum.oya-application-shell-frontend: Application control-plane SSR host: canonical Leptos/Axum router replaces the prior hand-rolled TCP/HTTP parser for the operator console. Read-only route graph: no server-function boundary is mounted, because the workspace declares zero `#[server]` functions and a wildcard POST over an empty registry would be an unauthenticated control plane. This is an SSR/control-plane surface, not a latency-critical data path. ADR-0090/ADR-0509 §6.
axum.oya-ci-webhook-gateway-app: CI webhook receiver: typed inbound webhook route surface (GitHub/HMAC) where axum extractors cut parsing/validation boilerplate; the crate ALSO uses hyper for upstream dispatch. NOTE: per the gateways-prefer-hyper bias this is a recorded MIGRATION CANDIDATE — the inbound receiver may move to bare hyper once the route surface stabilizes. Tracked, non-blocking. ADR-0374.
